title: United Airlines 826 (1997)

location.name: Pacific Ocean, about 870 nautical miles east-southeast of Narita

summary: United Airlines Flight 826, a Boeing 747-122, encountered severe clear-air turbulence at flight level 310 while operating from Tokyo to Honolulu on December 28, 1997. The aircraft experienced extreme accelerations of 1.814g positive and -0.824g negative, causing 1 fatality and 18 serious injuries among passengers and crew. The fasten seatbelt sign notification procedures were inadequate, leaving many passengers unrestrained during the event.
probable_cause: The pilot-in-command's inadvertent flight into adverse weather conditions, and the difficulty of obtaining adequate weather forecasts of over-ocean turbulence. Factors contributing to the accident included the presence of clear air turbulence and the failure of the flight attendant to issue a safety advisory.

factors.evidence: Severe clear-air turbulence encounter at FL 310 causing sudden drops and rolls; aircraft experienced peak acceleration of 1.814g and minimum -0.824g (p. 3)
Japanese-speaking flight attendant did not fully translate captain's fasten seatbelt instructions to Japanese passengers; passengers could not understand the safety advisory (p. 2, 3)
Difficulty communicating with non-English speaking medical doctors and passenger advisories due to language barriers (p. 3)
Aircraft suddenly dropped approximately 100 feet, rolled 18 degrees right, and dropped again with extreme negative G causing injuries and fatality (p. 3)

events.text: Flight at cruise altitude FL 310, about 870 nm east-southeast of Narita, Japan
Captain observed wave action and illuminated exterior lighting looking for clouds; no clouds visible; radioed NW 90 requesting ride report; NW 90 reported smooth ride with occasional light turbulence
Captain turned on fasten seatbelt sign as precaution after observing stars; customary public address announcements made in English and Japanese
First severe turbulence encounter: aircraft experienced wave action; captain indicated there were light green echoes on radar 50-60 miles ahead and right of course, no red echoes observed
Second severe turbulence encounter: aircraft dropped approximately 100 feet, pitched up, rolled 18 degrees right wing down with peak vertical acceleration 1.814g, then fell again with minimum -0.824g
Captain made PA announcement for flight attendants to sit down and told passengers not to be alarmed; ordered first officer to reduce speed to 330-340 knots

Cabin crew found flight attendant in aisle and cabin in disarray; multiple injuries identified; two doctors on board offered assistance; one doctor stayed with flight attendants performing CPR on unconscious passenger
Captain assessed injuries and airworthiness; decided to return to Narita rather than divert to Midway Island; used emergency authority to turn off course and climb 500 feet

Japanese passenger (seat 46F) died from injuries; received fatal cervical spinal injury; 15 passengers and 3 flight attendants sustained spine and neck fractures; 161 minor injuries among passengers and flight attendants

recommendations.text: Establish procedures to ensure effective communication of safety-critical information to non-English speaking passengers, particularly regarding fasten seatbelt requirements during cruise operations
Reinforce policies encouraging passengers to wear seatbelts whenever seated, regardless of seatbelt sign status
recommendations.outcome: United Airlines issued Flight Safety Information Bulletin 98-1 after the accident

safety_changes: United Airlines issued Flight Safety Information Bulletin 98-1 titled 'Turbulence Encounter and Passenger Fatality'
Emphasis on importance of effective communication between pilots and flight attendants
Measures to reinforce policy of encouraging passengers to wear seatbelts whenever seated

notes: Sections read: Factual Information (History of Flight, Injuries, Personnel), Analysis, Meteorological Information, Flight Recorders
Aircraft subsequently retired after accident; this was the aircraft's last revenue flight
Failure photoswitch in PA amplifier prevented low chime operation during fasten seatbelt sign illumination
